444+## 2. Flue — what we take and what we do not
445+
446+**Flue is `github.com/withastro/flue`** (Apache-2.0), an agent runtime by the
447+Astro team built on `pi-agent-core` — the same pi lineage as our
448+`pi-coding-agent`. It is a competitor to our *composition layer*
449+(`agent-host/`), not to our harness.
450+
451+### 2.1 What we DO NOT take: the runtime. Ratified, unchanged.
452+
453+`.../architecture/08-pluggable-agent-surfaces.md:296`, verified against source,
454+not merely judged:
455+
456+> "Not adopted — now verified, not just judged: mounting boring-agent *inside*
457+> Flue's runtime. Flue's LLM loop is a hardwired `new Agent(...)` from
458+> `pi-agent-core` inside its 125 KB `session.ts` — rich seams *around* the loop
459+> (tools, `SessionEnv`, model providers, execution interceptors) but **no seam
460+> at the loop**; hosting our pi-coding-agent harness means forking their core.
461+> Additionally: single flat `SessionEnv` per harness … and session persistence
462+> is an event-sourced SQL record log … incompatible with pi-coding-agent JSONL
463+> sessions. **Strategy: cherry-pick, don't adopt**."
464+
465+The memory eval reaches the same verdict independently: *"copy the Durable
466+Object pattern, defer celld, do not integrate Flue"* — because Flue "has no
467+tenancy/authorization story; adopting it = the 'second behavior composer' that
468+D25/D26/D28/D29 rejected four times."
469+
470+**Restated for this lane: we do not host our agent inside Flue, we do not adopt
471+`@flue/runtime`, and we do not adopt Flue's session persistence.**
472+
473+### 2.2 What we ALREADY took: the durable event store
474+
475+Our `SqliteEventStreamStore` **is a port of Flue's code**.
476+`docs/issues/807/runtime-refactor/work/T1-durable-events/TODO.md:14,57`
477+records the reference implementation and transaction requirement: Flue
478+`packages/runtime/src/runtime/event-stream-store.ts` (388 LOC) +
479+`handle-stream-routes.ts` (594 LOC). We renamed `flue_*` → `boring_event_*`
480+and fixed a real bug in the original: "Flue's `appendEvent` runs two
481+non-transactional statements… Wrap both in one transaction. Delete Flue's 'safe
482+for single-process' comment."
483+
484+That store is the substrate this whole lane stands on, and §5 proves it works.
485+
486+### 2.3 What we MAY take: `@flue/whatsapp` ingress — and the gap r2.1 left
487+
488+`08-pluggable-agent-surfaces.md:294`, verified at Flue `ffbe359`:
489+
490+> "the 13 per-channel ingress packages (`@flue/slack`, `teams`, `discord`,
491+> `telegram`, `github`, `linear`, `intercom`, **`whatsapp`**, `messenger`,
492+> `twilio`, `google-chat`, `zendesk`, `notion`) import **nothing from
493+> `@flue/runtime`** — dependencies are `hono` + provider type packages only.
494+> Apache-2.0. Each package provides: signature verification, provider-native
495+> payload parsing, Hono route handlers, and a self-contained
496+> `conversationKey`/`parseConversationKey` codec."
497+
498+This is **ratified as `docs/DECISIONS.md:302` decision 6**: "Use pinned
499+`@flue/*` ingress packages with thin adapters; vendoring is only the fallback
500+and hosting inside Flue's runtime is not adopted."
501+
502+**The gap (r2.1):** r2.1 chose Vercel's `@chat-adapter/whatsapp` for the
503+provider edge (via `cloudflare-channels-assessment.md`) and **never evaluated
504+`@flue/whatsapp` at all** — despite `@flue/*` being the *ratified* choice and
505+`@flue/whatsapp` being in the verified list.
506+
507+**Bake-off RESOLVED (2026-08-11).** The bake-off ran across all three
508+candidates. **Outcome: BUILD THIN, do not adopt any candidate wholesale.**
509+`@flue/whatsapp` gives only the inbound signature/webhook **edge** (~250
510+reusable LOC, Web-Crypto, invariant-clean) — near drop-in as a **seed**, but no
511+send/media/template/interactive. hermes-agent's `whatsapp_cloud.py` is the
512+best **correctness reference** (wamid dedup, 24h-window/template fallback, media
513+caps, formatting, conformance vectors) but is Python — a **port source**, not a
514+dependency. `@chat-adapter/whatsapp` is **rejected**: it is an adapter to
515+Vercel's `chat` runtime (Thread/`onNewMention`), so it drags in the very
516+thread-ownership model the ratified "pi owns the conversation brain" decision
517+rejected, and it uses `node:crypto`/`Buffer` (violates invariants #1/#2). The
518+saveable delta from any library is small (~600–750 LOC) and sits at the edge —
519+exactly what Flue seeds cleanly and Hermes documents. Slice 6 therefore builds
520+a ~600–750 LOC in-house adapter seeded from Flue (edge) + Hermes (reference).
521+
522+The r2.1 caveat is why no candidate is adopted wholesale — it is the acceptance
523+bar the in-house adapter still honors:
524+
525+> "we want the adapter package standalone behind our contract, **not** their
526+> Redis-state bot framework (their state/dedupe model would duplicate and fight
527+> our binding store and cursor semantics)."
528+
529+### 2.4 Cloudflare — assessed and rejected, unchanged
530+
531+`cloudflare-channels-assessment.md` stands: Cloudflare's own channel catalog has
532+**no WhatsApp and no SMS**; "on Cloudflare you would build the Meta Cloud API
533+webhook/send path yourself, exactly as on any VPS"; and "Cloudflare Inc is US
534+(CLOUD Act exposure regardless of data location) … Incompatible with Seneca's
535+'no US data path' positioning for message content."
536+
537+### 2.5 hermes-agent (NousResearch) — third bake-off candidate + dev-loop bridge
538+
539+`NousResearch/hermes-agent` (MIT, `github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent`; WhatsApp
540+docs at `hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/messaging/whatsapp`),
541+surfaced by the owner 2026-08-11. Four takes:
542+
543+1. **Bake-off outcome — correctness reference / port source (RESOLVED
544+ 2026-08-11).** Its WhatsApp **Cloud API adapter** (`whatsapp_cloud.py`, MIT,
545+ ~2,100 LOC Python) was evaluated as the third candidate and is the **most
546+ complete Cloud API reference** of the three — but it is Python, so it is not
547+ importable. Verdict: **port its correctness logic and conformance vectors**
548+ (wamid dedup, 24h-window/template fallback, media up/download + size caps,
549+ markdown→WhatsApp formatting) into slice 6's in-house TS adapter; use its
550+ `tests/conformance/vectors/whatsapp.json` as our test oracle. Not adopted as
551+ a dependency.
552+2. **Dev-loop option: the Baileys bridge.** hermes-agent also ships a
553+ **Baileys** bridge — unofficial WhatsApp-Web protocol emulation with QR
554+ pairing, no Meta Business account needed. Recorded as a **development-loop
555+ option only**: it lets us build and demo the channel end-to-end before
556+ Business verification (step 0's real long pole) completes. **Hard caveat:
557+ ban risk, unofficial protocol — NEVER for customer numbers or pilot
558+ production traffic.** Meta Cloud API direct remains the ratified production
559+ path (owner ruling, unchanged).
560+3. **Patterns worth lifting regardless of bake-off outcome:** their
561+ markdown→WhatsApp formatting converter (input to §3-shaping/slice 1b's
562+ dialect work) and their streaming-response **message-edit** pattern
563+ (progressively editing a sent message as the turn streams — to be evaluated
564+ against our completed-turns-only rule rather than assumed).
565+4. **Runtime verdict: same as Flue (§2.1).** Cherry-pick adapters and patterns;
566+ do **not** adopt the agent frame — no seam for our harness loop, no
567+ tenancy/authorization story, no approval gating.

571+## 3. Placement decision
572+
573+### 3.1 The contradiction that must be resolved
574+
575+Two ratified-ish positions conflict, and neither cites the other:
576+
577+- **`docs/DECISIONS.md` Decision 19, locked item 3** (ratified):
578+ "Channel/surface packages follow the **Flue-style package model** rather than
579+ `boring-agent` subpaths" — i.e. `packages/channels/<name>`. Decision 19 now
580+ carries a **“Current scope: Decision 28…”** banner that supersedes its
581+ dependency details while retaining package layering and named-consumer
582+ principles; this plan narrows only the retained surface-package placement.
583+- **`plan.md` r2.1 open question 1** (review-endorsed, owner-ungated):
584+ "`packages/agent/src/server/channels/`".
585+
586+### 3.2 Recommendation: split by trust boundary, honouring both
587+
588+**Channel CORE → `packages/agent/src/server/channels/` (r2.1 position).**
589+**Provider EDGE → `packages/channels/whatsapp` (decision 3 position).**
590+
591+The split is not a compromise; it follows from evidence:
592+
593+*Why the core must be inside `packages/agent`, in-process:*
594+1. It calls `HarnessPiChatService` directly and uses the event store's
595+ `subscribe` seam, which is an **in-process listener** (r2.1 decision 5:
596+ "A separate adapter process is not 'add workers later': it is a redesign").
597+2. It mints `AuthorizedAgentScope` — a trusted scope whose only legitimate
598+ minting authority is the host (`shared/gateway/types.ts:45`; consumed by
599+ `agent-host/types.ts`). A separate package
600+ minting scopes would either export the brand (unacceptable) or go through
601+ HTTP with its own tokens (the redesign above).
602+3. It needs `sessionKey(ctx, id)` to compute the stream path. That method is
603+ **private** today (`pi-chat/harnessPiChatService.ts:1412` at this plan's
604+ landing baseline), and r2.1 already requires
605+ "a **new exported resolver on the pi-chat service**". Exporting a resolver to
606+ an in-package consumer is a small seam; exporting it cross-package widens the
607+ public API surface for one caller.
608+
609+*Why the provider edge must be its own package:*
610+1. Decision 3 is ratified and the reasoning holds — provider SDKs, Hono route
611+ shims, and Meta-specific fixtures do not belong in the agent's dependency
612+ graph.
613+2. `cloudflare-channels-assessment.md` §4 already draws exactly this line:
614+ "slices 1a and 1b are invariant. **Only Slice 2's provider-transport edge is
615+ substitutable.**" Substitutable things go behind a package boundary.
616+3. The provider edge is **substitutable behind the contract** — the bake-off
617+ (§2.3, RESOLVED to build-thin) and any future provider swap must not touch
618+ the core.
619+
620+*Dependency rule* (from `08:312`): the provider-edge package depends on
621+`@hachej/boring-agent`'s **channel contract types only** — never on
622+`agent-host` internals, never on `HarnessPiChatService`. The core never imports
623+the provider package; the deployed host wires them together.
624+
625+**This reconciliation is an owner gate.** It is the only structural decision in
626+this plan that overrides an existing ratified decision, and it does so by
627+narrowing it (decision 3 continues to govern channel *packages*; it never
628+contemplated a channel *core* that mints scopes).
629+
630+### 3.3 No `packages/channels/shared` in this lane
631+
632+`08:299`: extract a shared package "**only when a second `@flue/*` channel
633+actually lands** (that second channel is the state trigger)". WhatsApp is the
634+first. The Hono→Fastify shim lives inside `packages/channels/whatsapp`.
635+
636+---
637+
638+## 4. Session routing: which host?
639+
640+### 4.1 Owner ruling (2026-08-11): WORKSPACE sessions on the app host
641+
642+Channel bindings target **workspace sessions on the app host** — the customer's
643+own workspace, the one created at signup with the default agent — **not** the
644+standalone single-agent host. This reverses the r3-draft recommendation below
645+(kept in §4.2 for the record, now describing the future headless tier).
646+
647+The owner's rationale is architectural, not incidental: **same session through
648+two doors.**
649+
650+1. **Deep-link continuity.** When the medium runs out (long quotes, document
651+ review, panes), WhatsApp can deep-link into the *running workspace session* —
652+ the customer opens the very session the channel is driving, rather than a
653+ copy in a separate headless deployment.
654+2. **Artifact drop collapses.** Because the recipient is an authenticated
655+ workspace member, artifact drop becomes *sharing links to workspace files
656+ rendered by the product's own viewers* — reuse the share-resource seam, no
657+ channel-side artifact store. See the shrunk slice 4.
658+3. **One approval intention, two surfaces.** Approvals surface in both WhatsApp
659+ and the workspace Inbox as a single intention (§6.1), not as a channel-local
660+ copy.
661+
662+**What this does NOT change.** Channel CORE placement in
663+`packages/agent/src/server/channels/` (§3.2) stands — the core is host-agnostic
664+and composes wherever the agent stack composes. The in-process **server-class
665+caller** requirement (§6.1) is likewise unaffected: the app host runs the same
666+`HarnessPiChatService`/`agent-host` composition in one process, so the channel
667+core mounts there exactly as it would have on the standalone host. The binding
668+row gains an explicit `workspaceId` alongside the session key, and sessions it
669+creates carry the typed `channel: 'whatsapp'` property (§6.4).
670+
671+*Why the old §4.2 objections no longer bind:*
672+- The channel's N per-binding tails are **in-process event-store listeners**
673+ (r2.1 decision 1), not browser HTTP streams — the hub's known
674+ connection-starvation problem (Chrome's 6-per-origin limit) is a browser-side
675+ phenomenon and does not apply to server-side subscribers.
676+- The webhook needs no browser auth or `x-boring-workspace-id` header: the
677+ channel core is a trusted in-process caller minting `AuthorizedAgentScope`
678+ from the binding row (r2.1 §2), resolving the workspace from the binding —
679+ the hub's browser machinery is bypassed, not fought.
680+
681+### 4.2 The standalone host: future headless tier (was the r3-draft pick)
682+
683+`createStandaloneAgentHostApp` remains **documented as the target for a future
684+headless tier** — deployments with no product workspace at all. It is not the
685+v1 ingress. Its §5 verification is *not* wasted: durable replay, cursor resume,
686+terminal events, prompt idempotency, and restart survival are properties of the
687+**shared substrate** (`HarnessPiChatService` + `SqliteEventStreamStore`) that
688+the app host composes identically, so §5 stands as the substrate proof for the
689+workspace-session routing too.
690+
691+**Tenancy consequence (supersedes the old one-workspace-scope caveat):** the
692+binding maps `(channel, conversationKey)` → `(workspaceId, sessionKey)` (opaque
693+key, §0.5.5). Tenant
694+separation is **per-workspace** — each customer's own signup workspace — not
695+per-session inside one shared scope. §7.3 item 4 is updated accordingly; the
696+one-number identity risks (items 1–3, 5) remain.
697+
698+### 4.3 Flag interaction — unspecified in r2.1, specified here
699+
700+`BORING_CHAT_DURABLE_STREAM` is **off by default**
701+(`buildAgentComposition.ts`), and the entire outbound path depends on it.
702+`BORING_AGENT_CHANNELS=1` with the durable stream off is a silently broken
703+deployment. **Boot-time assertion:** if channels are enabled and the durable
704+store is unavailable, fail boot loudly with a stable code, matching the
705+precedent already set by `f1e245be1` ("fail loudly when durable-stream flag is
706+on but store unavailable").
707+
708+---
709+
710+## 5. Substrate verification — the shared substrate works (run on the standalone host)
711+
712+Run on this VM, 2026-08-10, against **gemini-2.5-flash** through the repo's
713+existing custom-provider seam. Not a mock: real HTTP, real model, real sqlite.
714+
715+**Boot.** `createStandaloneAgentHostApp` requires a host-injected runtime
716+adapter (invariant 5 — workspace+sandbox swap as one pair); wired as
717+`dev.ts`/`bin/boring-agent.ts` do, with `createAgentSandboxRuntimeModeAdapter('direct')`
718+and `agentSandboxRuntimeHostOperations`.
719+
720+Model wiring used the **existing** `BORING_AGENT_CUSTOM_MODEL_*` provider seam
721+against Gemini's OpenAI-compatible endpoint — no code change:
722+
723+```
724+GET /api/v1/agents/default/models
725+{"models":[{"provider":"gemini","id":"gemini-2.5-flash","label":"gemini-2.5-flash",
726+ "available":true}],"defaultModel":{"provider":"gemini","id":"gemini-2.5-flash"}}
727+```
728+
729+**5.1 One real turn, end to end.**
730+
731+```
732+POST /api/v1/agents/default/sessions → 201 {"sessionId":"672ebadd-…"}
733+POST /api/v1/agents/default/sessions/:id/prompt
734+ {"requestId":"req-turn-1","clientNonce":"nonce-1","content":"Reply with exactly…"}
735+ → 202 {"accepted":true,"cursor":1}
736+```
737+
738+The ndjson event stream produced exactly the terminal-event contract r2.1's turn
739+assembler is specified against:
740+
741+```
742+seq 1 agent-start turnId turn:672ebadd-…:1
743+seq 2 message-start role user
744+seq 3 message-end
745+seq 4 message-start role assistant
746+seq 5 message-delta
747+seq 6 message-delta
748+seq 7 message-part-end
749+seq 8 message-end
750+seq 9 agent-end status: ok
751+```
752+
753+with the model's literal output `WHATSAPP_LANE_OK` in the deltas. **`agent-end`
754+with an explicit `status` exists and is the assembler's trigger.**
755+
756+**5.2 Cursor replay.** A fresh connection at `cursor=0` replayed all 9 frames;
757+`cursor=6` returned 3. Monotonic `seq`, resumable mid-stream.
758+
759+**5.3 Durable persistence.** With `BORING_CHAT_DURABLE_STREAM=1`, the store
760+opened at `<workspaceRoot>/.agent-event-stream.sqlite` and after one turn held:
761+
762+```
763+boring_event_streams 1
764+boring_event_stream_entries 9 ← matches the 9 stream frames exactly
765+boring_event_stream_keys 9 ← one idempotency key per event
766+```
767+
768+**5.4 Prompt idempotency.** Replaying the same `requestId` returned
769+`{"accepted":true,"cursor":1,"disposition":"prompt","duplicate":true}` — no
770+second turn. Note `requestId` is **required** by `PromptBodySchema` (a request
771+without it is a 400 `AGENT_COMMAND_INVALID_STATE`).
772+
773+**5.5 Restart survival — the decisive test.** Killed the process, restarted it
774+against the same store:
775+
776+- replay from `cursor=0` returned **all 9 frames**, including `DURABLE_OK`;
777+- a new prompt on the same session was accepted at **`cursor: 10`** — the stream
778+ continued rather than restarting;
779+- and the model answered the follow-up "what token did you just say?" with
780+ `DURABLE_OK`, proving **conversational memory survived the restart**, not just
781+ the event log.
782+
783+### 5.6 Verdict
784+
785+**The substrate is healthy.** (Run against the standalone host; per §4.2 the
786+properties proven here — durable replay, cursor resume, terminal events,
787+idempotent prompt, restart survival — belong to the shared
788+`HarnessPiChatService`/event-store stack the app host composes identically.) The
789+disconnected-and-asynchronous property that motivates this entire epic — a
790+consumer absent across a process restart resuming from a cursor with history
791+intact — is demonstrably already true.
792+
793+Three honest caveats, each a plan input rather than a blocker:
794+
795+1. **`BORING_CHAT_DURABLE_STREAM` is off by default.** Channels are the first
796+ component to require it in production → §4.3's boot assertion.
797+2. **The HTTP `/events` route does not expose the durable store.** Its `cursor`
798+ is a numeric index into the in-memory `PiChatReplayBuffer`, and cold open
799+ only rehydrates the last ~1000 events; beyond that a consumer gets
800+ `PI_CHAT_REPLAY_GAP`. This is exactly why r2.1 decision 1 has the adapter
801+ read `eventStore.readEvents` directly. **Confirmed correct — do not build the
802+ channel on the HTTP route.**
803+3. **`sessionKey` is private**, so nothing outside the service can compute a
804+ stream path. r2.1 already scoped the exported resolver; it is real work, not
805+ a formality.
806+
807+Repro recipe is in §9.
808+

810+
811+## 6. Architecture of the new v1 lanes
812+
813+### 6.1 Approval-in-WhatsApp (the ask-user machinery over WA)
814+
815+**What exists.** `plugins/ask-user/` is complete and rich:
816+`createAskUserTool` (`name: "ask_user"`), a typed question model
817+(`AskUserQuestion` with `questionId`, `sessionId`, `ownerPrincipalId`, `status`,
818+`schema`, `artifacts`, and a constant-time-compared **`answerToken`**), a form
819+schema of up to 8 fields (`text|textarea|select|multiselect|checkbox|radio|number`,
820+≤50 options, default 10-min / max 30-min timeout), and bridge ops
821+`ask-user.v1.{request,answer,cancel,pending,transcript}`.
822+
823+**What blocks us — precisely.** The bridge ops are caller-class gated:
824+`answer`/`cancel`/`pending` accept **`browser`** and **`server`** only. Over
825+HTTP (`POST /api/v1/workspace-bridge/call`) only two classes are reachable:
826+`runtime` (bearer token) and `browser` (hardcoded for cookie auth). So:
827+
828+> a runtime-token client can `request` but **cannot** `answer`; a browser client
829+> can `answer` but is scoped by `assertBrowserSessionScope` + `assertQuestionOwner`.
830+
831+**There is no headless HTTP path that enumerates and answers pending questions.**
832+`ask-user.v1.pending` returns *one* question, not a list, and the UI-state slot
833+`questions.pending` deliberately **omits `answerToken`**.
834+
835+**Design.** The channel is an **in-process `"server"`-class caller** holding the
836+same `AskUserStore`/`AskUserRuntime` instance. This is why §3.2 puts the core
837+inside `packages/agent`, running in-process with whichever host composes the
838+agent stack — under the 2026-08-11 ruling, the app host (§4.1), which the owner
839+confirmed leaves this requirement unaffected. The approval lane is the
840+requirement that makes the in-process placement non-negotiable. Per §4.1, the
841+same approval also surfaces as one intention in the workspace Inbox — WhatsApp
842+buttons and Inbox answer the same question, whichever lands first wins the
843+`askUserPending` CAS. No new public
844+HTTP surface, no `answerToken` on the wire, no second approval channel
845+(`08:284`: "Existing permission prompts and the ask-user plugin migrate onto
846+this path; no second approval channel").
847+
848+**Mapping to WhatsApp interactive messages.**
849+
850+| ask-user | WhatsApp | Constraint |
851+| --- | --- | --- |
852+| single `radio`/`select`, ≤3 options | interactive **reply buttons** | Meta caps at 3 buttons, 20 chars each |
853+| single `select`, 4–10 options | interactive **list** | Meta caps at 10 rows |
854+| `checkbox` (approve/reject) | 2 reply buttons | the owner-approval case |
855+| `text`/`textarea` | free-text reply | next inbound message is the answer |
856+| **multi-field forms (2–8 fields)** | **not expressible** | → deferral message: answer in the workspace |
857+
858+**Correlation is the hard part.** WhatsApp has no ephemeral messages and no
859+Slack-style `onAction` event — an interactive reply arrives as a *normal inbound
860+message* carrying the button's `id`. So:
861+
862+- the outbound interactive message encodes `{questionId, fieldId, optionIndex}`
863+ into the button `id` (opaque, ≤256 chars, **no `answerToken`** — the token
864+ stays server-side and is looked up from the binding's `askUserPending`);
865+- the drain worker checks `askUserPending` **before** treating an inbound as a
866+ prompt. An inbound that resolves a pending question is routed to
867+ `ask-user.v1.answer`, **not** to `prompt`;
868+- `askUserPending` is **consumed by exactly one inbound** (CAS), so a
869+ double-tapped button answers once — the r2.1 sketch, now load-bearing;
870+- a stale button (question already answered, cancelled, or timed out) gets a
871+ short "that request has expired" notice, never silence;
872+- an ask-user **timeout** (≤30 min) while the user is away is a normal cancel →
873+ failure notice out-channel.
874+
875+**Ordering hazard.** The turn assembler suppresses tool-call events (r2.1 §3),
876+yet ask-user detection lives in exactly those events. This was r2.1's stated
877+reason for demotion and it is real: the assembler must special-case ask-user
878+*without* leaking general tool chatter to the channel. This is the risk centre
879+of slice 3 and gets its own review budget.
880+
881+**Dependency:** this lane targets whatever seam `fix/786` lands
882+(`fix/786-human-intention-artifacts` is in flight and touches this machinery).
883+Slice 3 is sequenced after it merges; if it slips, slice 3 slips, and slices
884+1/2/4/5 are unaffected.
885+
886+### 6.2 Artifact drop (SHRUNK by the 2026-08-11 routing ruling)
887+
888+**Ruling effect first:** with bindings targeting the customer's own workspace
889+(§4.1), the WhatsApp recipient **is an authenticated workspace member**. The
890+owner's ruling collapses artifact drop to **sharing links to workspace files
891+rendered by the product's own viewers — reuse the share-resource seam, no
892+channel-side artifact store.** The r3-draft's "genuinely new public,
893+unauthenticated, expiring viewer origin" is therefore **out of v1 scope**; the
894+analysis below is retained because it documents why that surface was thought
895+necessary (it assumed a recipient with no account) and what still applies
896+(snapshot-on-publish for quotes, PDF rendering, WhatsApp document-message
897+delivery).
898+
899+**What exists — less than the name suggests.** `packages/agent/src/shared/share-entry.ts`:
900+
901+```ts
902+interface ShareEntryV1 { schemaVersion: 1; id: string; workspaceId: string;
903+ path: string /* SERVER-INTERNAL */; provenance: {...} }
904+interface ShareEntryStore { create; get; delete; list }
905+class InMemoryShareEntryStore implements ShareEntryStore
906+```
907+
908+plus `resolveShareEntry` (→ `ok | not_found | tombstoned`) and MCP exposure via
909+`shareResourceUri(id)` / `registerShareEntryResources`.
910+
911+**What is missing — be blunt about it.** The route `GET /a/:id`
912+(`server/http/routes/deepLink.ts`) is **workspace-membership-scoped**, and its
913+200 body is `{status:"ok", workspaceId, id}` — **it does not serve bytes at
914+all.** There is **zero** `publicUrl` / `signedUrl` / expiry machinery anywhere in
915+the repo. The only byte-serving routes are authenticated. And the AR1 lane
916+explicitly rules the other way: "The returned human link contains neither a
917+capability secret nor a workspace path; the authenticated member lands on the
918+destination-local copy" — i.e. AR1 links **require an authenticated session at
919+the destination**. *(r3-draft conclusion: "a WhatsApp recipient has no account,
920+AR1 is not our answer" — now inverted by §4.1: the recipient DOES have an
921+account, so the authenticated share-resource seam IS the answer.)*
922+
923+**So this lane builds a genuinely new surface.** Design constraints, taken from
924+the ratified artifact security posture in `08`:
925+
926+- tokens address **`artifactId + version + capability`, never workspace paths**
927+ (the PR #424 learning); `ShareEntryV1.path` is server-internal and must never
928+ appear in a URL;
929+- **snapshot-on-publish beats live-file access** — the PDF is frozen at send
930+ time, so a later workspace edit cannot retroactively change what a client was
931+ quoted. This is a correctness requirement for quotes, not just security;
932+- read-only, single-purpose, **expiring** (default 7 days, configurable),
933+ **revocable**, actor-attributed;
934+- served from a separate viewer origin with `CSP default-src 'none'`, no host
935+ cookies or storage, EU/CH blob storage.
936+
937+**Durability gap:** `ShareEntryStore` ships only as `InMemoryShareEntryStore`.
938+Links that die on restart are unacceptable for a quote sent to a client. A
939+sqlite-backed store is in scope for this slice.
940+
941+**PDF.** No PDF generation exists in the repo. Options, all EU/CH-safe because
942+they are local: headless-Chromium HTML→PDF (heavy dep, best fidelity, and the
943+design system already renders to HTML), or a typesetting path. Recommendation:
944+**HTML→PDF via headless Chromium**, reusing the product lane's quote template.
945+The CH-trades lane owns the template's content and layout; this lane owns only
946+"turn the rendered artifact into bytes behind an expiring link". Deliver the
947+link *and* the PDF as a WhatsApp **document** message, since Meta renders
948+document attachments inline and clients trust them more than a bare link.
949+
950+### 6.3 Inbound media
951+
952+**Photos — a short path exists.** `ChatAttachmentPayloadSchema`
953+(`shared/chat/piChatSchemas.ts`) is `{filename?, mediaType?, url, path?}`, max
954+20 per prompt, and `promptImagesFromAttachments` in `harnessPiChatService.ts`
955+accepts `data:image/*;base64,…` directly (magic-byte sniffed to
956+png/jpeg/gif/webp, capped by `MAX_PROMPT_IMAGE_BYTES`). So a downloaded photo
957+can reach the model **with no core change**.
958+
959+Three real constraints:
960+1. **Non-image attachments are silently dropped** from model input — they
961+ survive only as metadata. PDFs a client sends will *not* be read by the model
962+ in v1. Say so in the reply rather than pretending.
963+2. **`FollowUpPayload` has no `attachments`** — only the first prompt of a turn
964+ can carry media. A photo arriving mid-turn must open a new turn or be
965+ deferred; the drain worker must handle this explicitly.
966+3. Media must be fetched from Meta's Graph API by media-ID (short-lived,
967+ authenticated URLs), then stored **CH/EU-side** before use.
968+
969+**Voice notes — honest about transcription.** WhatsApp voice notes are OGG/Opus.
970+The repo has **no** file-transcription function. `plugins/live-transcription/`
971+exists but is *live dictation*: `whisperLiveKit.ts` / `kyutai.ts` take a browser
972+PCM stream over a WebSocket, gated to loopback/local authority. It is not a
973+"give me an audio blob, get text" API.
974+
975+Provider options, with jurisdiction stated plainly:
976+
977+| Option | Jurisdiction | Assessment |
978+| --- | --- | --- |
979+| **Self-hosted Whisper on our own VPS** (reuse `live-transcription`'s WhisperLiveKit compute) | **Ours — CH/EU, no third party** | **Recommended.** Message content never leaves our infrastructure, which is the same posture that made us reject Cloudflare. Cost is GPU/CPU time. Needs a new batch-file entry point beside the streaming one. |
980+| **Infomaniak** (CH) | **Swiss** | Already a first-class configured provider in `models/modelConfig.ts` (`readInfomaniakProvider`). Strong sovereignty fit **if** they expose a speech-to-text endpoint — verify before relying on it; today we use them only for chat completions. |
981+| OpenAI Whisper API | **US** | Rejected for message content. Same CLOUD Act reasoning that rejected Cloudflare. |
982+| Google / Gemini audio | **US** | Rejected for message content, for the same reason. |
983+
984+**Ruling for this plan: self-hosted Whisper, with Infomaniak as the fallback if
985+a Swiss managed endpoint is preferred operationally.** No US processor touches
986+WhatsApp message content. The privacy policy submitted in step 0.1 must name
987+whichever is chosen.
988+
989+Transcription is **attached as text**, with the original audio retained as a
990+stored artifact so a human can re-listen when the transcript is wrong.
991+
992+### 6.4 Channel as a first-class typed session property [GENERIC — see §0.5.2]
993+
994+**This is the generic `originChannel` mechanism (§0.5.2), described here in its
995+original WhatsApp framing.** Sessions carry a **typed channel identity**:
996+`originChannel: 'whatsapp'` for channel-originated sessions, `'web'` as the
997+default for everything existing; future channels (slack, email, excel) reuse the
998+same field rather than adding new mechanisms. This is a session property in the
999+shared session schema, not channel-local metadata. All three behaviors below are
1000+driven by looking up `registry[session.originChannel]` — the descriptor — not by
1001+branching on a channel name:
1002+
1003+1. **Badge** — the workspace session list shows a channel badge on
1004+ channel-originated sessions.
1005+2. **Filter** — the session list is filterable by channel.
1006+3. **Dialect shaping** — the §3-shaping dialect (WhatsApp markdown, 4096
1007+ chunking) is selected per session from this property, not hardcoded per
1008+ deployment.
1009+
1010+**Binding schema linkage, made explicit:** the `ChannelBindingStore` row links
1011+`(channel, conversationKey)` → `(workspaceId, sessionKey)` — where
1012+`conversationKey` is the opaque adapter-owned key (§0.5.5) — and the session that the
1013+binding creates (via the CAS create-race machine, §1.2b) is created **with**
1014+`channel: 'whatsapp'` set. The binding's `channel` column and the session's
1015+`channel` property are the same typed value — the binding is the addressing map
1016+(two-handles rule, §1.2c); the session property is the identity the workspace
1017+UI and the dialect shaper read. Slice 1a delivers both.
1018+
1019+### 6.5 Reopen-in-workspace — v1 READ-ONLY [GENERIC descriptor property — see §0.5.4]
1020+
1021+**Read-only-in-workspace is the descriptor field `sessionsReadOnlyInWorkspace`
1022+(§0.5.1), not WhatsApp UI code.** A channel-originated session **appears in the
1023+customer's workspace session list** (channel-badged from `descriptor.icon`,
1024+filterable per §6.4) and, when its descriptor has
1025+`sessionsReadOnlyInWorkspace: true` (WhatsApp does), **opens as a read-only
1026+transcript** using the existing read-only session idiom: full observability —
1027+WA inbounds as user turns, agent replies, tool runs — with **no send path from
1028+the workspace in v1**. The only workspace-side interaction is answering
1029+approval intentions via the Inbox (already planned, §6.1).
1030+
1031+This cuts the reopen requirement to **near-zero new UI**: the transcript
1032+renderer, session list, and read-only idiom all exist; slice 7 adds only the
1033+descriptor-driven badge/filter surfacing and the read-only gating for sessions
1034+whose descriptor sets `sessionsReadOnlyInWorkspace` (WhatsApp is the first such
1035+descriptor; the gate is `descriptor.sessionsReadOnlyInWorkspace`, not
1036+`channel === 'whatsapp'`).
1037+
1038+**Read-only is a per-deployment POLICY default, not channel nature (C1).** WhatsApp
1039+reopen is read-only in v1 because of the 24h-window/send-path asymmetry and the
1040+deferral of two-way takeover to v2 — not because a channel is intrinsically
1041+read-only. `sessionsReadOnlyInWorkspace` is a descriptor **default** a deployment
1042+can flip (a Slack channel with two-way reply is entirely plausible in v2). The
1043+plan states this as policy so the descriptor field is not mistaken for an
1044+intrinsic property.
1045+
1046+**Two-way human-takeover is v2** (slice 8). Its ready-made design sheet — the
1047+previously-flagged questions, parked not discarded:
1048+
1049+- **24h-window behavior:** the send API itself is symmetric (a human-typed
1050+ outbound uses the same send path and the same §7.1 window check/template
1051+ fallback as agent output); specify exact behavior inside vs outside the
1052+ window.
1053+- **Visible labeling:** human-typed messages are visibly distinguished from
1054+ agent output on both ends.
1055+- **Takeover semantics:** recommend the agent **yields while a human is
1056+ active** and **resumes on explicit handback**, not on a timer.
1057+
1058+### 6.6 Onboarding & identity [WA-SPECIFIC]
1059+
1060+#### Pilot (v1): provisioned bindings — NO identity build
1061+
1062+Under the pilot posture (§0.7), **identity is not built in v1.** A customer's
1063+number is provisioned during onboarding and bound to their pre-created
1064+workspace/session; an unknown inbound is fail-closed. There is no account
1065+minting, no phone-as-identity, no magic-link-over-WhatsApp on the pilot path.
1066+The customer's better-auth account already exists (created the normal way when we
1067+onboard them); the binding row simply points the channel at that account's
1068+workspace. **Everything below this line is Phase 2, not pilot.**
1069+
1070+---
1071+
1072+#### Phase 2 (product self-serve): TWO feasible signup flows — both buildable now
1073+
1074+> **Spike findings (2026-08-11) — read before this subsection.** The recovered
1075+> better-auth composition report
1076+> (`references/betterauth-spike-report.md`) records a better-auth **1.6.26** run
1077+> (npm resolved `^1.6.3`→`1.6.26`) through all five identity flows against a
1078+> real SQLite database. Its original harness was not committed, so Phase 2 must
1079+> recreate and automate the flows before implementation. It **corrects several assumptions that earlier drafts of this
1080+> section got wrong**, and its verdicts are folded in below. The headline
1081+> corrections: (a) `account.accountLinking` does **NOT** link phone to email —
1082+> it is social/OAuth-only, and phone lives on the `user` row, not as an account
1083+> provider; (b) there is **no user-merge primitive**; (c) placeholder replacement
1084+> is a stateful `changeEmail` workflow, **not** `updateUser`; (d) stock
1085+> magic-link delivered over WhatsApp is **not** safe phone proof — it asserts
1086+> email ownership and has destructive side effects. Phone identity is **feasible
1087+> but requires more custom orchestration than "enable a plugin".** Version caveat:
1088+> the magic-link single-use/revocation behaviors described are **1.6.26** and must
1089+> not be back-projected onto exact `1.6.3` — the deployed version must be
1090+> pinned/verified.
1091+
1092+Self-serve signup is **off the pilot critical path** but is **feasible now** in
1093+**two** forms — the product can offer whichever fits the discovery path. This
1094+supersedes the r4 draft's false "provider #4 / just a delivery adapter" framing
1095+**and** an earlier over-correction that called phone-first "genuinely hard, maybe
1096+never". The recovered better-auth composition report
1097+(`references/betterauth-spike-report.md`) plus the verified
1098+`@better-auth/core` `db/get-tables.ts` schema settle it: **phone-native signup
1099+is a tier-(b), moderate build via the `phoneNumber` plugin** — not hard, not
1100+deferred.
1101+
1102+**Flow 1 — Phone-native (WhatsApp-first) signup. Tier (b), moderate. Feasible.**
1103+This is the WhatsApp-native vision: *message us with your number → you're signed
1104+up.*
1105+- better-auth's **`phoneNumber` plugin** natively creates an account on phone-OTP
1106+ verification (`signUpOnVerification`). It is **not installed today** (adding it
1107+ is the build), but it is a first-class supported flow, not custom auth.
1108+- **WhatsApp is just the OTP transport.** The plugin's `sendOTP({ phoneNumber,
1109+ code })` callback is bring-your-own delivery (SMS today, WhatsApp is a different
1110+ transport). Delivering the OTP over WhatsApp is where the channel plugs in.
1111+ (Docs warn: do **not** `await` `sendOTP` — timing-attack risk.)
1112+- **The one friction — the placeholder email — has a built-in mechanism, but it
1113+ needs guarding.** Core `user.email` is `required: true, unique: true` (verified
1114+ verbatim in `db/get-tables.ts`; there is a maintainer `TODO(#9124)` to drop this
1115+ in v2, but our `^1.6.x` pin still requires it). The `phoneNumber` plugin fills it
1116+ via `signUpOnVerification.getTempEmail(phoneNumber)` — a deterministic
1117+ placeholder (e.g. `+15551234@placeholder.local`) derived from the unique number.
1118+ The spike confirmed the happy path (HTTP 200, one user + session, zero account
1119+ rows, `phoneNumberVerified=1`, `emailVerified=0`). **But the placeholder
1120+ namespace is NOT protected by better-auth**: the spike pre-claimed a predictable
1121+ placeholder via ordinary public email signup, and the later phone OTP
1122+ verification then failed HTTP **500 `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE`** with no phone
1123+ user created — a **phone-signup denial of service**
1124+ (`references/betterauth-spike-report.md`, Flow 1). **REQUIRED glue for
1125+ phone-native signup** (all confirmed by the spike):
1126+ 1. **Reserve the placeholder namespace/domain** so only the trusted
1127+ phone-derived flow may write it — fail-closed against user-controlled email
1128+ signup, email change, admin/import, and public magic-link initiation.
1129+ 2. **Canonical E.164 phone normalization** before lookup and placeholder
1130+ derivation, plus a phone validator.
1131+ 3. **Map a placeholder collision to a stable, recoverable application error**,
1132+ never a raw 500.
1133+ 4. Note: a phone-only user has **no credential account** and **cannot
1134+ password-login until enriched** (`changeEmail` + server-only `setPassword`).
1135+- **The placeholder is REPLACED by the real email at first payment** — collected
1136+ there already (§7.6 ladder / progressive-email). The mechanism is the
1137+ **`changeEmail` route, NOT `updateUser`** (`updateUser` returns HTTP 400
1138+ `EMAIL_CAN_NOT_BE_UPDATED` — spike Flow 2). The no-verification swap works
1139+ **only while the row is still unverified and `changeEmail.updateEmailWithoutVerification`
1140+ is enabled**; once the email is verified, real verification is required. And
1141+ because better-auth **hides collision to prevent enumeration** (`{status:true}`
1142+ can be a silent no-op), the caller MUST re-read user state after the call. This
1143+ is a small, stateful workflow — **not a merge, and not a plain `updateUser`.**
1144+
1145+**Flow 2 — Email-anchored (LP-discovered). Also feasible; cleaner on linking.**
1146+Identity keys on **email** (better-auth-native today) and WhatsApp is a linked
1147+channel:
1148+- **Flow 2a — web-discovered:** LP → email signup+verification (exists) → menu
1149+ offering "chat in web" or "link WhatsApp"; linking uses nao's **linking-code**
1150+ pattern (`/login <code>` from WhatsApp → link `whatsappNumber → userId`).
1151+- **Flow 2b — WhatsApp-discovered via signed round-trip token:** unknown-sender
1152+ bot replies with a web signup link carrying a **signed token encoding the
1153+ pending number** → user completes **email signup on web** → the token links the
1154+ number to the new account → success page returns to WhatsApp. The signed token
1155+ is the mechanism; it carries the number across the web hop.
1156+
1157+**Both valid; the product can offer phone-native (Flow 1) for `wa.me`-discovered
1158+users and email-anchored (Flow 2) for LP-discovered users.** `canOriginateIdentity`
1159+is opened for WhatsApp in both — the difference is only whether the minted account
1160+is phone-anchored (Flow 1, with a temp email) or email-anchored (Flow 2).
1161+
1162+**Honest caveats (spike-corrected — `references/betterauth-spike-report.md`):**
1163+- **`account.accountLinking` does NOT link phone ↔ email — it is social/OAuth
1164+ ONLY.** The spike's `link-social {provider:'phone-number'}` returned HTTP 404
1165+ `PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND`; **phone is stored directly on the `user` row, not as an
1166+ `account` provider** (spike Flow 3). Enabling `accountLinking` supplies **zero**
1167+ phone composition. Phone attachment must be MANUALLY orchestrated by the plan:
1168+ the **dedicated phone-attach route** (verify phone OTP with
1169+ `updatePhoneNumber=true` on an authenticated session) for the email-first
1170+ direction, and **`changeEmail` + server-only `setPassword`** for the phone-first
1171+ direction. `accountLinking` still governs **social-provider** linking on the
1172+ email side (Flow 2), and it is unconfigured today (`grep accountLinking
1173+ packages/core/src` → zero hits) — but it is **not** the phone mechanism.
1174+- **There is NO better-auth user-merge primitive (confirmed).** `Object.keys(auth.api)`
1175+ exposed no merge; two independent users stayed independent; attaching an
1176+ already-owned phone returned HTTP 400 `PHONE_NUMBER_EXIST` (and burned the OTP).
1177+ **Detach/reattach can TRANSFER a phone** (`updateUser({phoneNumber:null})` on the
1178+ source, fresh OTP on the target) **but does NOT merge users** — both rows survive
1179+ (spike Flow 4). A real merge is **custom transactional glue** (consolidate
1180+ users/accounts/sessions and every trades-domain FK, conflict rules, rollback).
1181+ It stays a **narrow tail: detect + support-assisted, never automated**, and is
1182+ kept **OFF the pilot/v1 path** — provisioned bindings (§0.7) avoid it entirely.
1183+- **Stock magic-link over WhatsApp is NOT safe phone proof.** `sendMagicLink`'s
1184+ transport is arbitrary, so WhatsApp delivery technically redeems — but
1185+ semantically stock `magicLink` treats **token possession as proof of the EMAIL**
1186+ even when no email was delivered. Worse, on an existing **unverified phone-first
1187+ user**, redemption on 1.6.26 set `emailVerified` false→true, **revoked prior
1188+ sessions**, and **DELETED the credential account** (spike Flow 5). So for
1189+ phone/WhatsApp proof the plan needs a **custom out-of-band challenge /
1190+ session-mint flow** — NOT stock magic-link delivered over WhatsApp. Stock
1191+ magic-link remains fine for web access **after** a real, verified email exists.
1192+
1193+**[UNVERIFIED — load-bearing] OTP templates skip the 24h window.** For a
1194+*business-initiated* WhatsApp OTP to a cold number (Flow 1's `sendOTP` over
1195+WhatsApp when the user has not messaged in-window), the send relies on Meta's
1196+**authentication-category** templates being window-independent — a claim that
1197+carries **no primary Meta-docs citation** (research file marks only pricing
1198+unverified). **Required gate before Flow 1's WhatsApp-OTP path is built.** If it
1199+does not hold, Flow 1 falls back to SMS OTP, or to Flow 2's web hop.
1200+
1201+**SMS fallback during the WABA ramp** (research §2, **[UNVERIFIED]** ~2,000/day
1202+figure). Auth-path only, never conversation content; a natural fallback for
1203+Flow 1's OTP if the WhatsApp-OTP window claim above does not hold.
1204+
1205+---
1206+

1210+capability (`canOriginateIdentity: true`, §0.5.1/§0.5.3). Two entry doors, one
1211+better-auth account. The diagram traces both signup paths, the link-into-session
1212+rule, the collision/merge case, and the point where the phone-native placeholder
1213+email is replaced by the real one at first payment (§7.6 ladder). Read
1214+`LP` = landing page (web), `WA` = `wa.me/<seneca-number>` (WhatsApp).

1249+ LINK --> CONV
1250+
1251+ CONV(["ONE better-auth account<br/>user id + phone on the user row<br/>+ email / google credential/social accounts"])
1252+
1253+ %% ---- Collision case (NO better-auth primitive) ----
1254+ COL["Collision: same person made TWO independent accounts<br/>(phone-first AND email-first, never in one session)"]
1255+ COL --> MERGE["CUSTOM transactional merge (no better-auth primitive):<br/>consolidate users/accounts/sessions + domain FKs,<br/>conflict rules + rollback; detect + support-assisted,<br/>NEVER automated. OFF pilot/v1 (provisioned bindings avoid it)"]
1256+ MERGE --> CONV
1257+
1258+ %% ---- Placeholder email replacement ----
1259+ CONV --> PAY{"First payment?<br/>(invoice / receipt / CH records)"}
1260+ PAY -->|"yes"| REPL["Placeholder email REPLACED by the REAL email<br/>via changeEmail route (NOT updateUser);<br/>no-verify swap only while unverified +<br/>updateEmailWithoutVerification; re-read state (hidden collision)"]
1261+ REPL --> CONV
1262+ PAY -->|"not yet"| CONV
1263+```
1264+
1265+Door B/b1 is Flow 1 (phone-native); Door B/b2 is Flow 2b (WhatsApp-discovered
1266+round-trip); Door A + linking code is Flow 2a (web-discovered). All three open
1267+`canOriginateIdentity` for WhatsApp; they differ only in whether the minted
1268+account is phone-anchored (b1, temp email) or email-anchored (b2 / A).
1269+
1270+#### Auth additions required — existing vs to-add
1271+
1272+**Does the existing default sign-in / sign-up need changes to support WhatsApp
1273+auth? Yes — and MORE custom orchestration than "enable a plugin".** The two
1274+web-first paths (Door A, and Door b2's LP hop) reuse the current better-auth stack
1275+verbatim. But WhatsApp-native signup (Door b1), cross-door phone/email
1276+composition, and merge each require concrete **custom** work. The spike
1277+(`references/betterauth-spike-report.md`) proved phone identity is **feasible** —
1278+phone-first accounts CAN be created and enriched into full email/password accounts
1279+on a single user id — but **not by flipping `accountLinking` on**. Honest effort
1280+framing: each addition below is a **moderate custom build**, and two of them
1281+(placeholder-namespace guarding, the OOB challenge) are custom glue better-auth
1282+gives no primitive for. This section **supersedes** any "just a delivery adapter /
1283+provider #4 is one config line" shorthand.
1284+
1285+**What exists today (verified 2026-08-11,
1286+`packages/core/src/server/auth/createAuth.ts`):** email/password
1287+(`emailAndPassword.enabled`), Google + GitHub OAuth (`socialProviders`), and the
1288+magic-link plugin whose `sendMagicLink` currently **renders an email and sends
1289+it over the email `transport`** (`renderMagicLink` → `transport.send`) — email-wired,
1290+keyed to email, not phone. There is **no `account.accountLinking`** configured
1291+(`grep accountLinking packages/core/src` → zero hits) and **no `phoneNumber`
1292+plugin** in the `plugins` array. **Spike-confirmed limits of the existing stack:**
1293+`accountLinking` is social/OAuth-only and cannot compose phone (Flow 3); there is
1294+no user-merge primitive (Flow 4); and stock magic-link over WhatsApp asserts email
1295+ownership with destructive side effects, so it is **not** a phone-proof mechanism
1296+(Flow 5).
1297+
1298+| Concern | Exists today | To add for WhatsApp auth (spike-corrected) |
1299+| --- | --- | --- |
1300+| Email/password sign-up | ✅ `emailAndPassword.enabled` | — (reused as-is by Door A / b2) |
1301+| Google + GitHub OAuth | ✅ `socialProviders` | — (reused as-is) |
1302+| Phone as an identity | ❌ **no** `phoneNumber` plugin | **(1)** install + configure the `phoneNumber` plugin; phone lands **on the `user` row**, not as an `account` provider. Includes `signUpOnVerification.getTempEmail` for the required-email field and `sendOTP` for WhatsApp OTP |
1303+| Placeholder-namespace guard | ❌ (unprotected → DoS, spike Flow 1) | **(2)** REQUIRED custom glue: reserve the placeholder domain (only the trusted phone flow may write it), E.164 normalization + phone validator, and map placeholder collisions to a stable recoverable error (never a raw 500) |
1304+| Phone↔email composition on one user | ❌ (NOT `accountLinking`) | **(3)** MANUAL orchestration, spike Flow 3: email-first → dedicated phone-attach route (verify OTP, `updatePhoneNumber=true`); phone-first → `changeEmail` + server-only `setPassword`. `accountLinking` does **not** do this |
1305+| Placeholder → real email | ❌ | **(4)** the **`changeEmail`** route (NOT `updateUser`); no-verify swap only while unverified + `updateEmailWithoutVerification`; re-read state (hidden collision). Small stateful workflow |
1306+| Web session from a phone account | ⚠️ magic-link is email-keyed & unsafe over WA (spike Flow 5) | **(5)** a **custom out-of-band challenge / session-mint** flow for phone/WhatsApp proof — do NOT deliver stock magic-link over WhatsApp (false email-verify + revokes sessions + deletes credential account). Stock magic-link stays for web access after a real verified email exists |
1307+| Social-side linking (Door b2) | ❌ `accountLinking` unconfigured | **(6)** enable/configure `account.accountLinking` (`trustedProviders`, `allowDifferentEmails`) for **email/social-side** linking only, plus a **signed round-trip token** binding the pending WhatsApp identity across the web hop |
1308+| Collision merge | ❌ **no primitive** | CUSTOM transactional merge (users/accounts/sessions + domain FKs, conflict rules, rollback). Detect + support-assisted, **never automated**; **OFF pilot/v1** (provisioned bindings avoid it) |
1309+
1310+**Net:** phone identity is feasible but is **six moderate custom additions**, not a
1311+config line — (1) `phoneNumber` plugin, (2) placeholder-namespace guard + E.164,
1312+(3) manual phone↔email composition, (4) `changeEmail`-based placeholder
1313+replacement, (5) a custom OOB challenge for phone-proof web sessions, (6)
1314+`accountLinking` for email/social-side linking + the Door-b2 signed round-trip
1315+token. The genuine account **merge** is a further custom, support-assisted tail
1316+with no better-auth primitive, kept off the pilot/v1 path. Nothing in the existing
1317+email/OAuth/magic-link paths is removed; WhatsApp/phone becomes an identity source
1318+on the same account model, at honest effort cost.
1319+
1320+#### Consumers of this identity mechanism
1321+
1322+The identity **mechanism** — the two-door signup, the reconciliation/merge rule,
1323+the six auth additions, and the progressive-email ladder — **lives here**, in
1324+the single WhatsApp plan, as the WhatsApp channel's identity-provider capability.
1325+Vertical **product** plans do not re-specify it; they **consume** it and
1326+reference this section:
1327+
1328+- **Trades / CH revenue agent (#1210)** consumes this mechanism for its
1329+ WhatsApp-native onboarding (its onboarding section references this §6.6 for
1330+ signup/identity rather than duplicating the model).
1331+- **Future verticals** likewise reference this §6.6; the mechanism is
1332+ channel/consumer infrastructure, the products are configuration on top.
1333+

1335+
1336+## 7. Risks
1337+
1338+### 7.1 The 24-hour customer service window — MUST be in the plan
1339+
1340+Meta permits free-form business replies **only within 24 hours of the customer's
1341+last message**. Outside it, free-form sends are rejected and only **approved
1342+template messages** may be sent.
1343+
1344+This is not an edge case for an agent channel — it is the normal case. A long
1345+research turn, a queued approval the owner answers the next morning, or a
1346+retry-after-park all land outside the window.
1347+
1348+Concretely:
1349+- the binding tracks `lastInboundAt`; the outbound worker checks the window
1350+ **before** every send;
1351+- inside the window: free-form;
1352+- outside: send the single approved UTILITY template (step 0.4) — "your agent
1353+ has an update, reply to continue" — which reopens the window when the user
1354+ replies, then deliver the held content;
1355+- **the pending content must not be discarded** while waiting; it stays at the
1356+ cursor and is delivered after the window reopens;
1357+- proactive/agent-initiated outreach beyond that one template stays **out of
1358+ scope** (r2.1, unchanged) — it is the fastest way to get a number banned.
1359+
1360+Cost note: template messages are billed per conversation; free-form replies
1361+inside a service window are not. A chatty agent that habitually falls outside
1362+the window is an expense, not just a UX problem.
1363+
1364+### 7.2 Meta policy compliance for business-initiated messages
1365+
1366+- v1 is **strictly user-initiated**. No lists, no imports, no broadcast.
1367+- Quality rating is per-number and degrades on user blocks/reports; a low rating
1368+ throttles then bans the number. **With ONE number for all tenants, one
1369+ tenant's users can degrade delivery for every tenant.**
1370+- Mitigations: the fail-closed unknown-sender policy (r2.1 §2 / §0.7,
1371+ rate-limited to once per sender — an unrate-limited auto-reply is itself a
1372+ ban risk), an explicit opt-out keyword (STOP) honoured before any agent
1373+ invocation, and monitoring of the quality rating as an operational alert.
1374+
1375+**Pilot avoids the account-minting abuse surface entirely.** Because the pilot is
1376+provisioned-bindings/fail-closed (§0.7), an unknown sender gets a rate-limited
1377+rejection and **nothing is minted** — no account, no workspace, no free LLM
1378+turns. The rate-limit above covers exactly the polite-rejection auto-reply.
1379+
1380+**Phase-2 abuse controls — REQUIRED before open signup ships (R5).** Open
1381+self-serve WhatsApp signup (§6.6 Phase 2) turns the Seneca number into a surface
1382+where **anyone of ~2B WhatsApp numbers** can mint a better-auth account +
1383+workspace + default agent + LLM turns, unauthenticated and free. The §7.2
1384+rate-limit above does **not** cover account-minting velocity. Before Phase-2
1385+signup is built, this section must gain: **per-number and GLOBAL signup caps**,
1386+**disposable/virtual-number-farm detection**, **cost caps on unpaid signup
1387+workspaces** (LLM-turn budget per un-converted account), and **signup-velocity
1388+alerting**. This is a required security section for Phase 2, not a v2 note — and
1389+it is one of the reasons the pilot deliberately stays fail-closed.
1390+
1391+### 7.3 One-number multi-tenant identity limits
1392+
1393+The owner's pilot ruling has consequences worth stating rather than discovering:
1394+
1395+1. **A phone number is the only identity we get.** No email, no verified name.
1396+ The binding table is the entire trust decision, and it is explicitly
1397+ provisioned (r2.1: "Bindings provisioned explicitly (CLI/admin op in v1)").
1398+ Someone who knows the number and is not provisioned gets the polite rejection.
1399+2. **One person = one binding = one session.** A user who works with two tenants
1400+ from one phone cannot be disambiguated. v1 accepts this; the binding is
1401+ `(channel, conversationKey, agentTypeId)` (opaque key, §0.5.5) and the pilot
1402+ must not assign one human to two tenants.
1403+3. **Number loss / SIM reuse.** A recycled number silently inherits a binding.
1404+ Bindings need an expiry/re-confirmation policy; v1 mitigates with revocable
1405+ status and the age alert from r2.1 open question 5.
1406+4. ~~Tenant separation is per-session inside one workspace scope~~ **Resolved
1407+ by the 2026-08-11 routing ruling:** bindings target each customer's own
1408+ signup workspace, so tenant separation is **per-workspace** (§4.2). The
1409+ former pilot limitation no longer exists.
1410+5. **The owner-approval flow assumes we know who the owner is.** With one
1411+ number, the approver is identified by *their own* binding, not by the
1412+ number — so approval routing needs an explicit `approverExternalId` on the
1413+ tenant config rather than being inferred.
1414+
1415+### 7.4 Engineering risks
1416+
1417+| Risk | Mitigation |
1418+| --- | --- |
1419+| `followUp` stranding (§1.2a) | `DrainCoordinator` in slice 1a, failing test first |
1420+| Duplicate outbound sends | Accepted and documented: at-least-once; no send idempotency key exists at Meta |
1421+| Turn assembler leaking tool chatter while detecting ask-user | Isolated in slice 3 with its own review budget |
1422+| Durable-stream flag off in prod | Boot assertion (§4.3) |
1423+| Any candidate library drags in a bot framework's state/dedupe model | RESOLVED (§2.3): build a thin in-house adapter (~600–750 LOC), seed the edge from `@flue/whatsapp`, port correctness from hermes-agent; reject `@chat-adapter/whatsapp` (runtime coupling + `node:crypto`/`Buffer`) |
1424+
1425+### 7.5 Magic-link web-auth security (owner addition, 2026-08-11)
1426+
1427+The magic-link (§6.6) is a **bearer token** — whoever holds the URL can
1428+establish the web session. It is **better-auth's magic-link token** (already
1429+wired, §6.6), so short-TTL and one-time-use are existing plugin behavior, not
1430+new code — we only choose the delivery channel. WhatsApp threads are
1431+forwardable, so keep the link hardened accordingly:
1432+
1433+- **Short TTL** — better-auth's magic link is minted at 10-minute expiry
1434+ (`createAuth.ts`); keep it minutes, not hours.
1435+- **One-time-use** — better-auth consumes the token on first successful
1436+ exchange; a second tap fails closed.
1437+- **Optional device/IP binding** — bind the token to the requesting device/IP
1438+ where feasible, so a forwarded link opened elsewhere is rejected.
1439+- **The auth basis is WhatsApp-as-possession-factor** — control of the number
1440+ is what authorizes minting the link in the first place; the link is a
1441+ short-lived hand-off of that already-proven possession, not an independent
1442+ credential. Phone OTP is the documented fallback with the same possession
1443+ basis.
1444+
1445+### 7.6 Billing & WABA ramp [WA-SPECIFIC] (owner addition, 2026-08-11; research-grounded)
1446+
1447+Billing is **not v1 build scope** — it is captured here so the identity
1448+trust-ladder (§6.6 progressive email) has a defined destination and the pilot
1449+does not discover these constraints late. Grounded in
1450+`references/whatsapp-auth-billing-research.md` §2–§3.
1451+
1452+- **Stripe Checkout at first payment.** Do not collect card details at signup.
1453+ The first-payment value moment (the same moment email becomes effectively
1454+ required, §6.6 ladder) triggers a **Stripe Checkout** session, which collects
1455+ the billing email and — for business customers — the **VAT/UID** number. This
1456+ keeps signup zero-friction and defers PII to when the customer chooses to pay.
1457+- **Swiss QR-bill is the required payment-slip format when a Swiss invoice uses
1458+ a payment slip.** It replaced the legacy slips; invoices settled by other
1459+ means do not inherently require one. Use the **`swissqrbill`** library;
1460+ it embeds the QR-IBAN, creditor reference, and amount.
1461+- **Swiss VAT = 8.1%** (standard rate, 2024+); invoices display the **UID**
1462+ (`CHE-###.###.###`, VAT-registered form). Stripe Tax / Checkout collects and
1463+ validates the VAT number at payment.
1464+- **Two data paths, kept separate.** Stripe is a US processor, acceptable for
1465+ payment PII the customer knowingly enters into a payment form — **distinct from
1466+ WhatsApp message content**, which stays CH/EU-side under the no-US-data-path
1467+ posture (§2.4, §6.3). The step-0 privacy policy states both paths.
1468+- **WABA messaging ramp** (research §2): the ~2,000 business-initiated
1469+ conversations/day cap on a fresh number, with the SMS-fallback mitigation for
1470+ the auth path (§6.6). Template messages are conversation-billed (§7.1); an
1471+ auth/OTP-heavy or out-of-window-chatty deployment is a cost line, not just UX.
1472+
1473+**Out of v1 build scope** (listed in §11): invoice generation, Stripe wiring, the
1474+QR-bill renderer, and SMS-provider integration. This note fixes the target shape
1475+so Phase-2 progressive-email collection (§6.6) lands on the right ladder.
1476+

1480+

1482+
1483+The epic branch adopts the smallest owner-requested pilot path from the broader
1484+r4.1 plan. The dependency graph is:
1485+
1486+```text
1487+plan landing (.9) → channel core/bindings/inbound (.2)
1488+ → durable tail/outbound/24h (.3)
1489+ ├─ in-chat owner approval (.5)
1490+ └─ thin Cloud API adapter + app-host wiring (.8)
1491+owner Meta review (.1) runs in parallel and gates only the live pilot receipt
1492+```
1493+
1494+Slices 1a-i/ii/iii are combined at the `.2` Bead's bounded core seam. Deployment
1495+wiring from historical slice 2 is included with `.8`. Artifact drop, inbound
1496+media, descriptor-driven workspace UI, self-serve identity, and two-way takeover
1497+(slices 4, 5, 7, 1c, and 8) are **not adopted for this execution epic**; their
1498+sections below remain design context, not dispatch authority. The current Bead
1499+graph is authoritative for execution and preserves fixture-backed progress while
1500+owner-owned Meta approval runs in parallel.
1501+
1502+**Full r4.1 design pipeline (historical/context):** `1a-i → 1a-ii → 1a-iii → 1b → {3, 4, 5, 7} → 6`; slices
1503+3/4/5/7 are parallel after 1b. **Slice 1c (identity) is Phase 2**, off the pilot
1504+critical path. Slice 8 is **v2**.
1505+
1506+**No signup on the pilot path.** Under the provisioned-bindings posture (§0.7),
1507+the pilot has **no account creation from inbound** — bindings are provisioned
1508+during onboarding to pre-created workspaces, and an unknown sender is fail-closed.
1509+So the pilot needs **no identity slice**; the binding row already targets an
1510+existing `workspaceId`. The old "slice 1c sits between 1a and 1b" sequencing is

1514+**Slice 1a is split into three PRs (C4).** The r4 monolithic 1a was three PRs in
1515+a trenchcoat (registry + descriptors + binding store + CAS create-race +
1516+DrainCoordinator + webhook core + CLI + boot assertion). Split:
1517+
1518+- **Slice 1a-i — `DrainCoordinator` + `followUp` fix (§1.2a).** Touches

1574+### Slice 1c — self-serve signup: phone-native and/or email-anchored [PHASE 2 — NOT pilot]
1575+**Not on the pilot critical path** (pilot = provisioned bindings, §0.7). Two
1576+**feasible** flows (§6.6), pick per discovery path; both buildable now:
1577+- **Flow 1 — phone-native (tier b, moderate):** add better-auth's `phoneNumber`
1578+ plugin (`signUpOnVerification`); deliver OTP via `sendOTP`→WhatsApp; use

1587+ exists; a custom phone-keyed token for earlier web access from a phone-native
1588+ account (moderate).
1589+**Custom glue (moderate, honest):** `accountLinking` matches on email not phone,
1590+so linking email/social onto a phone-first account and merging two independent
1591+accounts are custom (not built-in); the genuine merge is a narrow tail —
1592+detect + support-assisted, never automated. **Gated on** the Phase-2 abuse
1593+controls (§7.2 Phase 2) and (for Flow 1's cold-number WhatsApp-OTP) the
1594+`[UNVERIFIED]` OTP-window claim (§6.6) getting a Meta citation, else SMS fallback.

1596+**Proof (when built):** Flow 1 — an unknown number completing phone-OTP is signed
1597+up with a temp email, replaced by a real email at payment; Flow 2 — a WhatsApp
1598+number links onto an email account (no second account) and a tampered/expired
1599+signed token is rejected; no duplicate account for a returning linked user.

1601+### Slice 1b — durable tail, turn assembly, outbound
1602+**Delivers:** the exported stream-path resolver on the pi-chat service; the

1605+notice; stall timeout → notice + park); markdown→dialect shaping with 4096

1611+with cursor resume and zero duplicate sends; on hard crash between send and CAS,
1612+a duplicate is possible and asserted **not to be loss**; error/aborted/stalled
1613+turns always produce a notice, never silence; a permanently unsendable message

1628+
1629+### Slice 3 — approval in WhatsApp (ask-user over WA)
1630+**Delivers:** in-process `"server"`-class ask-user caller; ask-user detection in
1631+the turn assembler without leaking tool chatter; schema→interactive mapping
1632+(buttons ≤3, list ≤10, free-text, multi-field→deferral); button-id correlation
1633+codec; `askUserPending` CAS consumed-by-exactly-one-inbound; stale/expired/timeout
1634+notices.
1635+**Blocked by:** 1b **and** `fix/786` landing. **Own review budget.**
1636+**Proof:** an agent turn calling `ask_user` with a 2-option approval renders two
1637+WhatsApp buttons; tapping one resolves the question exactly once and the turn
1638+continues; double-tap answers once; a stale button gets an expiry notice; an
1639+8-field form renders the deferral message; `answerToken` never appears in any
1640+outbound payload (guard test); no phone number reaches an agent API (two-handles
1641+guard).

1643+### Slice 4 — artifact drop (SHRUNK 2026-08-11): share-resource links + PDF
1644+**Delivers:** artifact drop via the **existing share-resource seam** (§6.2) —
1645+links to workspace files rendered by the product's own viewers, opened by the
1646+authenticated workspace member the binding maps to. **Dropped from v1:** the
1647+channel-side `ShareEntryStore` durability work, the new public unauthenticated
1648+viewer origin, and the expiry/revocation link machinery — the recipient has an
1649+account, so authenticated links suffice. **Retained:** snapshot-on-publish for
1650+quotes (a later workspace edit must not change what a client was quoted);
1651+HTML→PDF rendering (headless Chromium, CH-trades lane owns the template);
1652+WhatsApp document-message send of the PDF alongside the link.
1653+**Blocked by:** 1b. Coordinates with the CH-trades lane for the quote template.
1654+**Proof:** a quote artifact produces a workspace share link that opens in the
1655+product viewer for the bound customer; the sent PDF is the snapshot, unchanged
1656+by a later workspace edit; no workspace path or capability secret appears in
1657+the URL or the document filename.
1658+
1659+### Slice 5 — inbound media
1660+**Delivers:** Meta media-ID download; CH/EU-side storage; photos → prompt
1661+attachments via the existing image path; **batch-file transcription entry point
1662+beside `live-transcription`'s streaming one** (self-hosted Whisper); transcript
1663+attached as text with original audio retained; explicit honest reply for
1664+unsupported types (PDFs etc., per §6.3 constraint 1); mid-turn media policy
1665+(`FollowUpPayload` has no attachments).
1666+**Blocked by:** 1b. **Proof:** a photo sent on WhatsApp reaches the model and is
1667+described back; a voice note is transcribed and answered; a sent PDF gets the
1668+honest "I can't read documents yet" reply rather than silence; no media bytes
1669+transit a US processor (documented data path).
1670+
1671+### Slice 6 — WhatsApp provider edge (Meta Cloud API) — BUILD THIN (bake-off RESOLVED 2026-08-11)
1672+**Verdict (was "evaluate 3 candidates"):** the bake-off ran and resolved to
1673+**build a thin in-house Cloud API adapter (~600–750 LOC)** seeded from two
1674+sources, **not** adopt any candidate wholesale. Full analysis in §2.3/§2.5.
1675+
1676+**Today (bake-off result):**
1677+- `@chat-adapter/whatsapp` (Vercel Chat SDK, MIT) is **REJECTED** — reasons all
1678+ architectural, none about quality (it is in fact the most actively maintained
1679+ candidate). It is an adapter to Vercel's `chat` **runtime** (the
1680+ Thread/`onNewMention` conversation model), not a standalone Cloud client, so
1681+ adopting it means adopting that thread-ownership model — a direct collision
1682+ with the ratified **"pi owns the conversation brain"** decision (the pi-native
1683+ cutover already rejected `useChat`-style thread ownership). It also uses
1684+ `node:crypto` + `Buffer`, violating shared invariants #1/#2, and its most
1685+ "mature" features (24h-window awareness, threading) are exactly the logic
1686+ **our plan deliberately owns** — pure coupling cost for behavior we override.
1687+- `@flue/whatsapp` (Apache-2.0, ~430 LOC) provides **only the inbound webhook /
1688+ signature edge** (~250 reusable LOC) — Web-Crypto based (**no `node:*`, no
1689+ `Buffer`**, workerd-safe), matching `src/shared` invariants #1/#2 near
1690+ drop-in. It has **no** outbound send, media, templates, or interactive.
1691+- hermes-agent's `whatsapp_cloud.py` (MIT, Python, ~2,100 LOC) is the **most
1692+ complete Cloud API correctness reference** but not importable — value is as a
1693+ port source and correctness oracle (it ships conformance test vectors).
1694+
1695+**Delta — what slice 6 now builds:** `packages/channels/whatsapp` behind the
1696+contract, hand-built in TypeScript against `@whatsapp-cloudapi/types`:
1697+- **Seed the inbound webhook/signature edge from `@flue/whatsapp`** (Apache-2.0,
1698+ keep the NOTICE attribution) — `x-hub-signature-256` HMAC via Web Crypto,
1699+ `hub.verify_token` constant-time compare, `hub.challenge` handshake,
1700+ body-limit + envelope guard.
1701+- **Port the Cloud API correctness logic + conformance test vectors from
1702+ hermes-agent's `whatsapp_cloud.py`** (MIT, Python→TS): wamid dedup, the
1703+ 24h-window / template-fallback shape, media upload + 2-step download with
1704+ per-type Meta size caps, markdown→WhatsApp formatting, text batching. Its
1705+ `tests/conformance/vectors/whatsapp.json` becomes our test oracle.
1706+- Write our own ~250 LOC of Graph-API send + media helpers.
1707+- Reliability-critical state (binding dedup, cursor semantics, turn assembly,
1708+ the authoritative 24h-window enforcement) stays in **our** plan (slices
1709+ 1a/1b), never in the adapter — this is why no candidate's bot-framework
1710+ state/dedupe model is adopted.
1711+**Blocked by:** 1b for the contract; **step 0** for the live demo only. The
1712+build feeds 1a/1b (it realizes the `ChannelAdapter` provider edge they define).
1713+**Proof:** ported conformance vectors green for verify/parse/chunk/template/
1714+media; no `node:*` or `Buffer` in the package (invariant guard); live demo
1715+against the Seneca number — a multi-message conversation spanning a server
1716+restart, with one approval answered in WhatsApp and one quote PDF delivered.
1717+
1718+### Slice 7 — read-only reopen in workspace (new, 2026-08-11)
1719+**Delivers:** §6.5/§0.5.4 — **descriptor-driven** session-pane rendering: channel
1720+icon badge + channel filter read from `registry[session.originChannel]` (§6.4),
1721+no per-channel UI code; sessions whose descriptor sets
1722+`sessionsReadOnlyInWorkspace` (WhatsApp is the first) open as **read-only**
1723+transcripts via the existing read-only session idiom (send path gated on
1724+`descriptor.sessionsReadOnlyInWorkspace`, not a channel-name check); full
1725+transcript renders (WA inbounds as user turns, agent replies, tool runs).
1726+Near-zero new UI by owner design. This slice delivers the generic mechanism's
1727+pane rendering with WhatsApp as its first descriptor.
1728+**Blocked by:** 1b (needs the channel property + real transcripts). Parallel
1729+with 3/4/5.
1730+**Proof:** a WA session appears badged in the customer's session list, filters
1731+by channel, opens read-only with the full transcript; the composer is absent/
1732+disabled with no send route reachable (guard test); Inbox approvals for that
1733+session still work (§6.1).
1734+
1735+### Slice 8 (v2) — two-way human-takeover
1736+**Not v1.** Typing into a channel session from the workspace delivers to the
1737+WhatsApp counterpart — human-takeover as a feature. Carries §6.5's design sheet
1738+as its input: symmetric send path with §7.1 window/template handling, visible
1739+labeling of human vs agent messages on both ends, agent yields on takeover and
1740+resumes on explicit handback. Scoped and sequenced when v1 has shipped.

1744+## 9. Repro recipe for §5
1745+
1746+```bash
1747+cd /home/ubuntu/projects/boring-ui-v2/.worktrees/playground-main
1748+export BORING_CHAT_DURABLE_STREAM=1
1749+export BORING_AGENT_SESSION_ROOT=/tmp/wa-ws/sessions
1750+export BORING_AGENT_CUSTOM_MODEL_PROVIDER=gemini
1751+export BORING_AGENT_CUSTOM_MODEL_ID=gemini-2.5-flash
1752+export BORING_AGENT_CUSTOM_MODEL_BASE_URL=https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai
1753+export BORING_AGENT_CUSTOM_MODEL_API_KEY=<vault: secret/agent/gemini field api_key>
1754+export BORING_AGENT_DEFAULT_MODEL=gemini:gemini-2.5-flash
1755+```
1756+
1757+Boot script (needs the host-injected runtime adapter — see §5):
1758+
1759+```ts
1760+const R = '<repo>/packages/agent/src'
1761+const { createStandaloneAgentHostApp } = await import(`${R}/server/createStandaloneAgentHostApp`)
1762+const { agentSandboxRuntimeHostOperations, createAgentSandboxRuntimeModeAdapter }
1763+ = await import(`${R}/../host/sandbox.ts`)
1764+const app = await createStandaloneAgentHostApp({
1765+ mode: 'direct',
1766+ runtimeModeAdapter: createAgentSandboxRuntimeModeAdapter('direct'),
1767+ runtimeHost: agentSandboxRuntimeHostOperations,
1768+ workspaceRoot: process.env.WA_WS, sessionId: 'default', logger: false,
1769+})
1770+console.log(await app.listen({ port: 5458, host: '127.0.0.1' }))
1771+```
1772+
1773+Drive it (`requestId` and `clientNonce` are required):
1774+
1775+```bash
1776+B=http://127.0.0.1:5458
1777+SID=$(curl -s -X POST $B/api/v1/agents/default/sessions \
1778+ -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"requestId":"c1"}' \
1779+ | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["sessionId"])')
1780+curl -sN "$B/api/v1/agents/default/sessions/$SID/events?cursor=0" &
1781+curl -s -X POST "$B/api/v1/agents/default/sessions/$SID/prompt" \
1782+ -H 'content-type: application/json' \
1783+ -d '{"requestId":"t1","clientNonce":"n1","content":"Reply with exactly: DURABLE_OK"}'
1784+```
1785+
1786+Kill the process, rerun the boot script, and replay `?cursor=0` — all frames
1787+return and the next prompt continues the stream.

1793+1. **Placement split (§3.2)** — **RESOLVED 2026-08-11**: the owner's routing

1795+ (host-agnostic)". Core in `packages/agent/src/server/channels/`, provider
1796+ edge in `packages/channels/whatsapp`; DECISIONS.md decision 3 is narrowed
1797+ accordingly on merge.
1798+2. **Transcription provider (§6.3)**: self-hosted Whisper (recommended) vs
1799+ Infomaniak, pending confirmation that Infomaniak offers speech-to-text. Names
1800+ a sub-processor in the step-0 privacy policy, so it must be decided before
1801+ step 0 is submitted.
1802+3. ~~Share-link expiry default~~ — **MOOT 2026-08-11**: the public expiring
1803+ bearer link is out of v1 (§6.2 shrink); share-resource links are
1804+ authenticated workspace links with no bearer-expiry question.
1805+4. **Approver identity (§7.3 item 5)**: confirm `approverExternalId` per tenant
1806+ is the right v1 model for "owner approves in WhatsApp".
1807+5. **Slice 3 sequencing**: confirm slice 3 waits for `fix/786`, and that slices
1808+ 1/2/4/5 shipping without in-channel approval (deferral message meanwhile) is
1809+ an acceptable intermediate state.
1810+6. **Governance**: this plan reverses the 2026-08-08 deprioritization in
1811+ `docs/direction/STATE.md`. That file needs updating on approval.
1812+
1813+## 11. Out of scope
1814+
1815+**Self-serve WhatsApp signup (phone-native and email-anchored) + account merge** —
1816+these are **Phase 2**, not v1 (§0.7, §6.6, slice 1c). Both signup flows are
1817+feasible now (phone-native = `phoneNumber` plugin, tier (b) moderate;
1818+email-anchored = `accountLinking`), but the pilot uses provisioned bindings
1819+(fail-closed) and mints no identity, so it needs none of them, no
1820+account-minting abuse controls, and no merge. Phase-2 signup is gated on the §7.2
1821+Phase-2 caps and (for Flow 1's cold-number WhatsApp-OTP) a primary Meta-docs
1822+citation for the OTP-window claim. Automated account merge stays out of scope
1823+(no better-auth primitive; support-assisted only).
1824+
1825+**Any future consumer's implementation** — Slack, email, and pi-excel channels
1826+are **registry-ready future consumers, noted only** (§0.6); this plan builds
1827+**zero** of them (the mechanism proves generic without them, and
1828+`demo/pi-excel-coupling` already demos the coupling). Also out: SMS as a
1829+conversation channel (SMS appears only as the auth-OTP fallback, §6.6/§7.6);
1830+group chats; per-agent grant policy (#1087); proactive outreach beyond the single
1831+fallback template; multi-agent routing per sender; horizontal adapter scale-out;
1832+**billing build-out** (Stripe Checkout wiring, invoice/QR-bill generation, VAT
1833+handling, SMS-provider integration — §7.6 fixes the target shape only);
1834+billing/metering of channel traffic; two-way human-takeover from the workspace
1835+(v2, slice 8); the standalone headless-tier deployment (§4.2); model-readable
1836+inbound PDFs (§6.3); per-customer Embedded Signup /
1837+replies-on-customer's-own-number (§0, §6.6 — separate future capability); the
1838+CH-trades product surface (separate lane).
