39 ▸ docs/issues/1127/references/whatsapp-auth-billing-research.md docs added +99 −0
@@ -0,0 +1,99 @@
1+# WhatsApp auth + billing research
2+
3+Grounding evidence for the WhatsApp consumer's identity model (plan §6.6, §7.5,
4+slice 1c) and its billing note (plan §7.6). Produced during the #1127 / PR #1211
5+grounding pass (2026-08-11) and checked in here as durable evidence rather than
6+left in scratchpad. Findings that could not be verified against a primary source
7+are flagged `[UNVERIFIED]` inline.
8+
9+Scope note: this file grounds the **WhatsApp consumer**, not the generic channel
10+mechanism. Auth (OTP vs magic-link) is WhatsApp-consumer-specific; the generic
11+`canOriginateIdentity` capability flag is what the mechanism exposes.
12+
13+---
14+
15+## 1. WhatsApp auth — authentication-template window behavior is unverified
16+
17+**[UNVERIFIED — load-bearing]** This secondary-research claim has no primary
18+Meta documentation citation in the repository. It must be verified before the
19+Phase-2 WhatsApp OTP path is built; otherwise use SMS OTP or the web round trip.
20+
21+- Authentication-category message templates (OTP / one-time-passcode templates)
22+ appear to be a distinct category from UTILITY and MARKETING. The working
23+ hypothesis is that they can be business-initiated without an open 24-hour
24+ customer-service window, allowing an OTP to reach a cold number.
25+- Auth templates support the **copy-code** and **one-tap** button types. The
26+ **copy-code** button is the low-friction default: the user taps "Copy code",
27+ the code is placed on the clipboard, they paste it back.
28+- Recommended **OTP TTL: 10 minutes** — matches better-auth's default magic-link
29+ / verification-token expiry, so the WhatsApp delivery adapter and the auth
30+ layer agree on lifetime without extra config.
31+- Consequence for the plan: the **channel-as-verifier** path (first inbound
32+ proves control of the number) remains the primary, zero-template signup path;
33+ the **OTP auth-template** path is the documented fallback that also works
34+ business-initiated (e.g. the "get login link / code on WhatsApp" reverse flow
35+ when the user is on the web login page and has not yet messaged us).
36+
37+`[UNVERIFIED]` exact per-region auth-template pricing; treated as
38+conversation-billed like other template categories (see §3).
39+
40+---
41+
42+## 2. SMS fallback during WABA ramp
43+
44+While the WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) quality tier ramps, per-number
45+messaging limits apply:
46+
47+- **[UNVERIFIED]** A newly-verified number reportedly starts in a low messaging
48+ tier capped at ~2,000 business-initiated conversations/day until quality and
49+ volume raise the tier. User-initiated replies inside a service window do not count against this
50+ the same way, but business-initiated OTP/login sends do.
51+- **Mitigation: SMS fallback for the auth OTP/login path during the ramp.** If a
52+ WhatsApp auth send is throttled or the number is not yet on WhatsApp, fall back
53+ to an SMS OTP through a CH/EU-jurisdiction SMS provider. This keeps signup/login
54+ working while the WABA tier climbs, and is auth-path-only (never for agent
55+ conversation content, which stays WhatsApp-native).
56+- This is a **WhatsApp-consumer-specific** operational concern; it does not touch
57+ the generic channel mechanism.
58+
59+---
60+
61+## 3. Billing — Stripe Checkout at first payment, email + VAT, Swiss QR-bill
62+
63+Billing enters the model at the **first payment** value moment (plan §6.6
64+progressive-email ladder makes email effectively required here).
65+
66+- **Stripe Checkout at first payment.** Do not collect card details at signup.
67+ Trigger a **Stripe Checkout** session at the first payment moment; Checkout
68+ collects the email and billing details Stripe needs. This aligns with the
69+ progressive-email ladder — email becomes required exactly when billing does.
70+- **Email + VAT collected at Checkout.** Swiss/EU invoicing needs a billing
71+ email and, for business customers, a **VAT/UID number**. Stripe Tax /
72+ Checkout can collect and validate these.
73+- **Swiss QR-bill is the standardized format when an invoice uses a Swiss
74+ payment slip.** It replaced legacy payment slips; an invoice settled by other
75+ means does not inherently require one. Use the **`swissqrbill`** library to
76+ generate the QR-bill when that payment method is offered. The QR-bill embeds the creditor
77+ reference, IBAN (QR-IBAN), and amount.
78+- **Swiss VAT rate: 8.1%** (standard rate, 2024+). Invoices show the **UID**
79+ (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer, `CHE-###.###.###` formatted with the
80+ `MWST`/VAT suffix for VAT-registered entities).
81+- **Data path:** Stripe is a US processor. Card/billing PII flowing through
82+ Stripe Checkout is acceptable (it is payment data the customer knowingly enters
83+ into a payment form), and is **distinct from WhatsApp message content**, which
84+ stays CH/EU-side under the no-US-data-path posture (plan §2.4, §6.3). Keep the
85+ two data paths separate and say so in the privacy policy.
86+
87+`[UNVERIFIED]` exact Stripe Tax coverage for every CH edge case; confirm QR-IBAN
88+vs standard-IBAN reference-type at implementation time.
89+
90+---
91+
92+## 4. How these findings land in the plan
93+
94+| Finding | Lands in |
95+| --- | --- |
96+| **[UNVERIFIED]** OTP auth-templates bypass the 24h window; 10-min TTL copy-code | §6.6 identity (gated fallback path), §7.5 security, slice 1c |
97+| SMS fallback during WABA ramp (2000/day cap) | §7.6 billing/ramp note, §7.2 policy |
98+| Stripe Checkout at first payment; email+VAT | §6.6 progressive-email ladder, §7.6 |
99+| Swiss QR-bill (`swissqrbill`), 8.1% VAT, UID | §7.6 billing note |

41 ▸ docs/issues/1127/references/betterauth-spike-report.md docs added +88 −0
@@ -0,0 +1,88 @@
1+# better-auth 1.6.26 phone-identity spike — recovered report
2+
3+**Run date:** 2026-08-11
4+**Recovery date:** 2026-09-04
5+**Scope:** Phase-2 identity research only; not required by the provisioned-binding pilot
6+**Source receipt:** [PR #1211 §6.6 identity-corrections comment](https://github.com/hachej/boring-ui/pull/1211#issuecomment-5252253841)
7+
8+This is the durable report that the reviewed plan cited but PR #1211 omitted.
9+It records the observed outcomes preserved in the owner-authored receipt and the
10+r4.1 plan. The original scratch workspace and executable spike harness were not
11+committed, so this file is **not a reproducible test bundle**. Re-run these flows
12+against the exact deployed better-auth version before implementing Phase 2.
13+
14+## Composition under test
15+
16+- better-auth `1.6.26` (resolved from the then-declared `^1.6.3` range)
17+- real SQLite database
18+- `phoneNumber` plugin with `signUpOnVerification`
19+- email/password, social-provider linking, `changeEmail`, `setPassword`, and
20+ magic-link APIs as applicable to each flow
21+
22+Version caveat: these observations describe `1.6.26`. In particular, do not
23+back-project magic-link session/account side effects onto exact `1.6.3`; pin and
24+re-test the deployed version.
25+
26+## Observed flows
27+
28+### Flow 1 — phone signup and placeholder collision
29+
30+The happy path created one verified-phone user and session with the temporary
31+email supplied by `getTempEmail`; it created no `account` row and left email
32+unverified. A phone-only user therefore had no credential account and could not
33+use password login until enriched.
34+
35+Pre-claiming the deterministic placeholder through ordinary email signup caused
36+later phone verification to fail with HTTP 500 / `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE`; no
37+phone user was created. better-auth did not reserve that namespace. Phase 2 must
38+reserve the placeholder domain, normalize and validate E.164 input, and map a
39+collision to a stable recoverable error.
40+
41+### Flow 2 — replace placeholder email
42+
43+`updateUser` returned HTTP 400 `EMAIL_CAN_NOT_BE_UPDATED`. The supported path was
44+`changeEmail`. A no-verification replacement worked only while the old email was
45+unverified and `changeEmail.updateEmailWithoutVerification` was enabled.
46+better-auth may hide a collision behind a successful-looking response to avoid
47+account enumeration, so callers must re-read user state after the change.
48+
49+### Flow 3 — phone/email composition
50+
51+`link-social` with `{provider: "phone-number"}` returned HTTP 404
52+`PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND`. Phone identity lives on the `user` row rather than in an
53+`account` provider row, so `account.accountLinking` does not compose phone and
54+email.
55+
56+The resulting design seam is manual orchestration: email-first users attach a
57+phone through authenticated OTP verification with `updatePhoneNumber=true`;
58+phone-first users add email/password through `changeEmail` plus server-only
59+`setPassword`. Social/OAuth linking remains a separate `accountLinking` concern.
60+
61+### Flow 4 — collision and transfer are not merge
62+
63+No user-merge API was present. Attaching a phone already owned by another user
64+returned HTTP 400 `PHONE_NUMBER_EXIST` and consumed the OTP. Detaching then
65+reattaching could transfer the number, but both user rows survived; it did not
66+merge users, workspaces, sessions, or domain records.
67+
68+A real merge therefore remains custom transactional work with explicit survivor,
69+foreign-key, conflict, audit, and rollback rules. It is off the pilot path and
70+must be support-assisted rather than automatic.
71+
72+### Flow 5 — stock magic-link is not phone proof
73+
74+Delivering a stock email-keyed magic link over WhatsApp made token possession act
75+as proof of the email address. On the tested unverified phone-first user,
76+redemption changed email verification state, revoked prior sessions, and removed
77+the credential account. The stock magic-link flow must not be used as proof of
78+phone/WhatsApp possession. A phone-proof web session requires a separate
79+out-of-band challenge/session-mint design; stock magic links remain suitable only
80+after a real email is verified.
81+
82+## Implementation gate
83+
84+These findings size and constrain a possible Phase-2 identity slice. Before that
85+slice is dispatched, recreate the harness in-repo, pin the exact better-auth
86+version, and turn each outcome above into an automated regression. The v1 pilot
87+requires none of these flows because unknown senders fail closed and bindings are
88+provisioned.
42 ▸ docs/issues/1127/show-me-plan.md docs added +84 −0
@@ -0,0 +1,84 @@
1+# WhatsApp Channel — plan, visually
2+
3+**Status:** Gate 1 candidate
4+**Epic:** `whatsapp-channel` · `wt-391-forward-1127-channels-plan-4fv`
5+**Canonical plan:** `plan-whatsapp.md` r4.1, with `plan.md` r2.1 and `references/*`
6+**TL;DR:** Add one channel-neutral registry/core, prove it end-to-end with a fake channel, then connect a thin provisioned-only WhatsApp Cloud API edge.
7+
8+## Structure — where responsibility lives
9+
10+```text
11+packages/
12+├── agent/src/server/channels/ # registry, descriptors, bindings, inbound/outbound workers
13+├── agent/src/server/events/ # existing durable stream consumed by channel tail
14+├── agent/src/server/pi-chat/ # session turns and exported stream-path resolver
15+└── channels/whatsapp/ # thin Meta verify/parse/send adapter only
16+
17+docs/issues/1127/
18+├── plan.md # r2.1 durable channel foundation
19+├── plan-whatsapp.md # r4.1 owner-ruling delta and WhatsApp execution plan
20+└── references/ # provider/auth research provenance
21+```
22+
23+## Behavior — one durable conversation through two asynchronous directions
24+
25+```mermaid
26+sequenceDiagram
27+ participant Person as WhatsApp user
28+ participant Edge as Cloud API edge
29+ participant Core as Channel core
30+ participant Agent as Workspace agent
31+ participant Store as Durable event store
32+
33+ Person->>Edge: signed inbound message
34+ Edge->>Core: verified normalized inbound
35+ Core->>Core: atomic dedupe + enqueue
36+ Core-->>Edge: fast acknowledgement
37+ Core->>Agent: prompt or followUp in bound session
38+ Agent->>Store: append turn events
39+ Core->>Store: tail from persisted cursor
40+ Core->>Core: assemble terminal turn
41+ Core->>Edge: free-form reply or 24h template
42+ Edge-->>Person: outbound message / approval choices
43+ Person->>Core: approval answer
44+ Core->>Agent: resolve one Human Intention
45+```
46+
47+## Change shape — dependency-correct execution graph
48+
49+```diff
50+ [WhatsApp Channel] Epic
51++├── Land the reviewed plan (.9)
52++│ └── Build channel core, bindings, inbound (.2)
53++│ └── Build durable tail, turn assembly, outbound, 24h (.3)
54++│ ├── Enable in-chat owner approval (.5)
55++│ └── Build thin Cloud API adapter (.8)
56++└── Complete Meta App Review submission (.1, owner-owned, parallel)
57+```
58+
59+Meta approval gates only the live pilot receipt; recorded fixtures keep adapter implementation and proof unblocked.
60+
61+## Decisions and boundaries
62+
63+| Decision | v1 choice | Why |
64+|---|---|---|
65+| Identity | Provisioned pilot bindings; unknown senders fail closed | Avoids open-signup/auth and abuse risk |
66+| Durability | Direct durable-store tail with persisted cursor | UI replay is retention-window bounded |
67+| Delivery | Outbound at-least-once; cursor CAS after send | Meta has no idempotency key; no-loss is honest |
68+| 24-hour rule | Free-form inside window, one approved utility template outside | Matches Cloud API constraints |
69+| Approval | `ask_user` choices and exactly-once answer through channel | Owner can approve without opening Workspace |
70+| Provider edge | Thin in-house adapter behind generic core | Keeps provider behavior out of session orchestration |
71+| Adopted execution subset | No self-serve signup, media, artifact drop, descriptor UI, or human takeover | Identity/takeover remain Phase 2/v2; media, artifact drop, and descriptor UI remain in the broader r4.1 design but are not dispatch authority for this epic |
72+
73+## Proof and risk
74+
75+| Risk | Mitigation / proof |
76+|---|---|
77+| Duplicate or lost inbound | Atomic dedupe+enqueue, restart and create-race tests |
78+| Long-offline outbound gaps | Durable replay test from persisted cursor |
79+| Duplicate outbound after crash | Explicit at-least-once contract; CAS prevents cursor divergence |
80+| Expired WhatsApp reply window | Template-fallback test |
81+| Cross-tenant identity error | Provisioned-only lookup, fail-closed unknown sender test |
82+| Meta review delay | Fixture-backed exchange; owner-owned review lane runs in parallel |
83+
84+Gate 2 requires workspace and agent suites green, invariants green, a recorded fake-channel end-to-end run, and a live pilot-number exchange receipt if Meta review has cleared.
43 ▸ docs/issues/1127/references/getnao-auth-study.md docs added +76 −0
@@ -0,0 +1,76 @@
1+# getnao / nao auth study
2+
3+Grounding evidence for the identity model (plan §6.6 two-flow model, slice 1c).
4+External validation for better-auth's internal-user plus linked social/credential
5+account shape and nao's messaging linking-code UX. The later composition spike
6+clarified that phone identity itself lives on the `user` row and is **not** an
7+`account` provider; see [`betterauth-spike-report.md`](betterauth-spike-report.md).
8+Produced during the #1127 / PR #1211 grounding pass (2026-08-11).
9+
10+---
11+
12+## 1. nao runs the same stack we extend — better-auth validation
13+
14+nao (`getnao` / nao) authenticates on **better-auth** (`^1.6.3`), the same
15+library boring-core already mounts (`createAuth.ts`). Observed:
16+
17+- **Internal-id user model with linked accounts.** better-auth's
18+ `user` + `account(providerId → userId)` tables support one internal user with
19+ linked credential/social accounts (Google, GitHub, email/password).
20+- **`accountLinking.enabled`.** nao enables better-auth account linking for its
21+ supported social/OAuth providers.
22+
23+Takeaway: the internal-user/social-account shape is proven, but it does **not**
24+make phone “provider #4.” The 1.6.26 spike found that phone is stored directly
25+on the user row; phone↔email attachment therefore needs the manual orchestration
26+specified in plan §6.6.
27+
28+---
29+
30+## 2. nao's linking-code pattern (plan Flow A)
31+
32+nao links an external messaging identity to an existing web account via a
33+**short, regenerable linking code**:
34+
35+1. Authenticated web user requests a linking code (short, human-typable,
36+ regenerable — a new one invalidates the old).
37+2. User opens the messaging channel and sends `/login <code>` (or equivalent).
38+3. Backend resolves the code → `userId`, then records the messaging identity
39+ against that authenticated user through application-owned linking logic.
40+
41+This is the plan's **Flow 2a** (web-first → link WhatsApp). It is the right UX
42+shape for connecting a messaging identity to an existing account, but better-
43+auth `accountLinking` alone does not attach a phone.
44+
45+---
46+
47+## 3. The single-use-verification-token warning (why Flow B differs)
48+
49+The critical negative finding — do **not** copy nao's linking-code shape for
50+web-session establishment:
51+
52+- nao's **linking code is long-lived and reusable** by design (it is convenient
53+ to keep a code around to re-link). That is acceptable for a one-time identity
54+ **link** — the worst case is linking the same identity again.
55+- **It is a security bug as a *session* credential.** A long-lived, reusable code
56+ that mints a *web session* is a session-token-that-never-expires — anyone who
57+ sees the code (forwarded WhatsApp message, shoulder-surf) can open a session,
58+ repeatedly.
59+- **Therefore a WhatsApp-first web-session flow must use a short-lived,
60+ single-use out-of-band challenge**, not nao's reusable linking code and not
61+ stock email magic-link semantics. The 1.6.26 spike found unsafe side effects
62+ when stock magic-link was treated as phone proof; see the recovered report.
63+
64+The plan therefore keeps linking and session establishment distinct: Flow 2a
65+may use a regenerable code to link an identity, while phone-proof web access
66+requires a purpose-built, single-use challenge/session-mint flow.
67+
68+---

76+| Reusable-code warning for session establishment | §6.6 custom OOB challenge, §7.5, slice 1c |

1+# WhatsApp Channel — what changed at `e45248ade`
2+
3+## Runtime shape
4+
5+```diff
6++ apps/full-app
7++ ├─ config + credential lease ───────────────────────────────┐
8++ └─ /api/channels/whatsapp/webhook │
9++ ▼
10++ packages/core app host ── packages/agent channel runtime ── Meta edge
11++ ├─ durable binding, inbound queue, dedupe, leases
12++ ├─ completed-turn assembly + cursor-fenced outbound
13++ ├─ in-chat approval claim/answer routing
14++ └─ restart reconciliation + fail-closed revocation
15++
16++ packages/channels/whatsapp
17++ ├─ raw-byte HMAC + challenge verification
18++ ├─ WhatsApp parse/render + 4096-safe chunking
19++ └─ Graph text/template sends + bounded retry
20+```
21+
22+## Shipped flow
23+
24+```mermaid
25+sequenceDiagram
26+ participant Meta
27+ participant Webhook
28+ participant Store
29+ participant Agent
30+ participant Outbound
31+ Meta->>Webhook: signed inbound message
32+ Webhook->>Store: atomic dedupe + enqueue
33+ Store-->>Webhook: durable receipt
34+ Webhook-->>Meta: 200 acknowledgement
35+ Store->>Agent: prompt or follow-up
36+ Agent->>Store: durable completed-turn events
37+ Outbound->>Store: tail from fenced cursor
38+ Outbound->>Meta: text chunks or 24h template
39+ Outbound->>Store: compare-and-set cursor
40+```
41+
42+## Clean-install CI shape
43+
44+```diff
45+ build:packages
46+ build packages/agent
47++ build packages/channels/*
48+ build packages/core
49+
50+ lint
51++ resolve @hachej/channel-whatsapp from its built package entry
52++ validate the intentional Agent Host channel-runtime exports
53+```
54+
55+## Review boundaries
56+
57+```diff
58++ Provisioned senders only; unknown/removed senders fail closed
59++ Feature unreachable when BORING_AGENT_CHANNELS is off
60++ Inbound: durable exactly-once enqueue by provider message ID
61++ Outbound: at-least-once send, cursor fenced after delivery
62++ Outside 24h: approved utility template fallback
63++ Owner approval: claim-fenced answer routing in chat
64+- Self-serve channel signup
65+- Horizontal adapter scale-out
66+- Live Meta pilot before owner App Review clears
67+```

5353 {"id":"wt-391-forward-16f.2","title":"16f.2 BYOK vault storage: KmsBackend + OVH-KMS default + local-KEK fallback","description":"Add the dedicated credential schema/store and envelope crypto. Per-workspace 256-bit DEK, AAD-bound AES-256-GCM per the research brief (12-byte random nonce, 16-byte verified tag, canonical versioned AAD = workspaceId:credentialId:providerId:fieldId:credentialVersion:dekGeneration). KmsBackend abstraction (WorkspaceKekProviderV1: generateDataKey/unwrapDataKey/rewrapDataKey/readiness, fail-closed-on-unavailable) with OVHcloud KMS as the DEFAULT managed-EU-KMS impl (external-kms-opaque.v1 payload; REST/KMIP client-cert auth; region-pinned) and an explicit LOCAL-KEK dev fallback (sealed host file, separate from DB). Scaleway/Exoscale are alternate managed-EU-KMS impls of the same interface; self-run Vault/OpenBao Transit is optional. Dev-infra Vault at 100.77.36.113 is NOT prod. Write-only/masked (last-4 metadata only), timing-safe comparisons, no-secrets-in-logs, query logging disabled for credential tables. Owner-ratified 2026-07-20 amendment A.\n\nAcceptance gates (plan 'Cryptographic conformance'): raw Postgres inspection finds no plaintext canary/DEK/KEK/OAuth code-or-token/auth header; known-answer/round-trip per backend; corrupt ciphertext/nonce/tag/AAD/EDK/backend-ID/key-ref/key-version each independently fail closed CREDENTIAL_UNREADABLE/backend error (never 'absent'); nonce-uniqueness assertion + forbid zero/static nonce and unauthenticated modes; workspace-A row/EDK copied to B, provider-A->B, field-A->B, version-A->B all fail auth; wrong/missing KMS/local key is unreadable and never triggers another backend or instance fallback; backend conformance for OVH-KMS primary and local-KEK (sealed-file fixture, verified wrapper tag, rotation/rewrap, startup failure without key, no env fallback).","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","created_at":"2026-07-20T21:01:27.901694511Z","created_by":"claude-opus","updated_at":"2026-07-20T21:02:22.078692976Z","source_repo":"wt-820-beads","source_repo_path":"/home/ubuntu/projects/boring-ui-v2/.worktrees/wt-820-beads","compaction_level":0,"original_size":0,"labels":["391","820"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"wt-391-forward-16f.2","depends_on_id":"wt-391-forward-16f","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-07-20T21:01:27.901694511Z","created_by":"claude-opus","metadata":"{}","thread_id":""},{"issue_id":"wt-391-forward-16f.2","depends_on_id":"wt-391-forward-16f.1","type":"blocks","created_at":"2026-07-20T21:02:22.077271107Z","created_by":"claude-opus","metadata":"{}","thread_id":""}]}
